newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Arafat cautious on Mideast breakthrough.
newsitem.headline: Arafat cautious on Mideast breakthrough.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Wednesday played down talk of a breakthrough in the stalled Middle East peace process.

"Nothing was achieved yesterday," Arafat told a news conference the day after he met Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy and they reopened the Middle East peace talks that had been in limbo since April.
"I am looking to achieve something concrete. We are not asking for the moon," Arafat said after meeting Belgian Foreign Minister Eric Derycke.
"We are asking for what has been signed at the White House to be implemented completely and successfully," he added, referring to the "land for peace" agreement that launched the peace process.

Arafat's comments were in stark contrast to confident remarks earlier by Levy after he met Manuel Marin, the European Commissioner with responsibility for relations with the Middle East and Development Aid.
"I am satisfied that things will change. We have entered a period of cooperation that I am sure will have good results," Levy told reporters.
